decision: Replace the keyless djb2 reachable from applyTransform(_, 'hash') with a per-tenant keyed digest threaded through a new optional KeyedDigest port on ResolverDeps (the established GrantSource/ClassificationSource/EffectSource/SodSource injected-port pattern). The port (src/core/keyed-digest.ts) computes HMAC-SHA256 over a canonical length-prefixed preimage of (tenantId, resourceType, facetField, valueStr) keyed by a secret silo key, returning a hex digest or undefined when no key is available for the tenant; node:crypto/process.env live ONLY in this port, never in the pure data-classification core (FF-DC9). MaskContext gains additive optional resourceType/tenantId/keyedDigest members; maskFields' hash branch calls ctx.keyedDigest(...) and OMITS the key (drop) when the port is absent (D-4/AC-6) or returns undefined (no key, D-3/AC-5), never emitting the keyless digest and never revealing raw. tenant_id is threaded from the already-validated handle.tenantId (grant-resolver.ts:460), not re-fetched. Q-arch custody = env_secret: the per-silo secret CHOROS_MASK_DIGEST_KEY is read once at the composition root (src/main.ts, the only process.env boundary, honest-degrade like buildLifecycleDepsFromEnv) and bound into the port; NO DB key table, NO migration 032 — because a DB-custodied key lives in the same Postgres the masking defends (circular custody) and the silo model needs only one secret per silo (T-0061 .env.prod.example REPLACE_WITH_* required-form). AC-13 (DB-custody isolation) is therefore not applicable / skipped.

rejected_alternatives.why_not: Circular custody — the key would live in the same Postgres instance the masking defends; a DB read that exposes masked output can also expose the key, collapsing the keyed property back to keyless. Adds a migration + RLS table + per-tenant key lifecycle for no security gain over a silo env secret under silo-only delivery. AC-13 is conditional on this and is skipped.

rejected_alternatives.option: Keep digest() keyless but salt it with tenant_id only
rejected_alternatives.why_not: D-2: tenant_id is non-secret (appears in handles, logs, RLS GUCs). Offline rainbow/dictionary attack survives — anyone who knows the tenant_id (everyone) brute-forces low-entropy values. A secret must participate (C-2).
Breaks the deterministic-token property (T-0033 AC-13) and the legitimate within-tenant mask-join/dedup use (D-1). The transform exists to be a deterministic token, not a nonce.
Violates C-4 / FF-DC9 — the pure core must import no node:crypto/process.env. The keyed digest is a capability behind an injected port; the bound digest function is passed in via MaskContext.

rejected_alternatives.option: Add a second handle->fields export carrying the digest
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Violates C-5 / FF-DC7 / FF-DC17 single-resolver invariant. The keyed digest rides the existing ONE maskFields/projectFields call via MaskContext; no second resolution edge.

rejected_alternatives.option: Reuse audit-preimage.ts createHash('sha256') directly for masking
rejected_alternatives.why_not: That is an UNKEYED SHA-256 audit-chain preimage (no secret) — using it for masking re-introduces the rainbow attack (C-2). The masking port needs a KEYED HMAC; only the node:crypto precedent is borrowed, not the unkeyed construction.

rejected_alternatives.option: Reversible encryption / tokenization with reversible key custody
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Out of scope (T-0033 §6-A #12 gold-plating); hash stays non-reversible (spec §7).
